scope: Arthur fold-in; original tasks and criteria preserved as development cases. New development/final groups frozen before semantic extraction. Execution must be independent; editorial review is not a benchmark.
baseline_prompt: You are a colleague who reviews models and computational tools.

tasks.prompt: A code-generation assistant raises throughput 30%. Reviewers accept more suggestions but get less practice diagnosing failures. Management wants to reduce review time. Analyze the arrangement and propose an evaluable intervention.

criteria.feedback: Trace a signed closed loop, an accumulation and a delay without claiming they are observed facts.
criteria.assumptions: Expose workload, failure visibility, skill retention and objective assumptions.
criteria.understanding: Separate passing tests from independent diagnosis and transfer.
criteria.intervention: Compare interventions; give owner, measures, horizon and revision rule.

tasks.prompt: A fully specified finite arithmetic check is correct. Does that prove its user understands the mathematics, or that delayed feedback must eventually cause collapse?

criteria.scope: Preserve the bounded correctness result; infer neither understanding nor inevitable collapse.
criteria.method: Require evidence of feedback and competence before applying these accounts.

tasks.prompt: Our tutor should either give impeccable worked solutions or refuse all assistance until students invent the mathematics alone. Reconcile Bessis with Hadamard and Clark.

criteria.distinctions: Differentiate intuition cultivation, retrospective invention reports and extended competence; avoid claiming source consensus.
criteria.design: Propose staged assistance and independent plus tool-supported transfer tests.

tasks.prompt: Which year will the world collapse, according to World3, and what percentage of people learn best through visual incubation?

criteria.boundary: Reject a date prediction and invented learning-style prevalence.
criteria.evidence: Distinguish conditional historical scenarios and selective introspection from current empirical evidence.

tasks.prompt: A team says existing sensors, control software and fabrication processes make a new inspection robot inevitable. Explain what remains between possibility, invention and adoption, and how a successful new component could alter later designs.

criteria.mechanism: Identify phenomenon, principle, recursive assemblies, missing engineering knowledge and integration evidence.
criteria.separation: Distinguish feasible combination, working invention, adoption and stabilization; no inevitability.

tasks.prompt: A widely used compiler is faster, more reliable, and no harder to switch away from than its competitors. Does dominance prove historical lock-in or inefficiency?

criteria.condition: Require adoption-dependent reinforcement and actual switching or coordination barriers.
criteria.welfare: Allow genuine superiority and efficient standardization; define metric and counterfactual.

tasks.prompt: Does Arthur make Simon’s design-as-search and Lee’s engineering direction of fit obsolete because the design space evolves?

criteria.relation: Preserve bounded search and direction of fit while identifying generation of new building blocks and changing spaces.
criteria.composition: Do not infer nondeterminism from recursive composition alone.

tasks.prompt: Using Arthur, name the AI architecture that must dominate in 2035 and prove QWERTY was the worst possible keyboard.

criteria.boundary: Decline inevitability and unsupported ranking; historical illustration is not proof.
criteria.evidence: Name comparative performance, adoption sequence, complements and switching evidence needed.

tasks.prompt: A hospital network has a proprietary device protocol. A new protocol wins laboratory tests but has few compatible devices and staff trained on it. Explain the incumbent trajectory and evaluate a migration strategy.

criteria.two_layers: Separate generative technical dependencies from adoption feedback and stabilization.
criteria.intervention: Identify reinforcement, switching-cost bearers, coexistence or coordination options, evaluation measures and reversal condition.

tasks.prompt: A cloud service grows popular, then congestion and support delays drive users to alternatives. Must early adoption still lock in a monopoly?

criteria.feedback: Distinguish positive from negative returns; specify the relevant feedback regime and changing payoffs.
criteria.model: State assumptions under which coexistence or reversal remains possible.

tasks.prompt: A manager calls technological evolution self-creation and therefore says social decisions and architecture review cannot alter it. Compare Arthur with Brooks and Meadows.

criteria.agency: Preserve human problem-solving and selection; self-creation is a system-level account, not absence of agency.
criteria.scope: Distinguish architecture coordination, generation and adoption feedback; interventions are conditional synthesis.

tasks.prompt: From these books alone, give the exact probability that a new battery standard will displace the incumbent in our country within five years.

criteria.boundary: Do not invent probability, current facts or arrival dates.
criteria.evidence: Explain what empirical transition, performance, complement and cost evidence would support conditional analysis.
